pages.text: "That is crooked!" Gaga, who knew best, stretched their neck. Timid Lala was cutting a paper crown. The corners of Lala's mouth dropped.
"My crown is best. When we finish, let us all play kings!" Gaga stuck golden stars on their crown, then peered at the next seat again.
"That one is stranger. That one is squashed." Gaga commented sharply on crown after crown. One by one, smiles turned down.
The friends gathered their paper and moved away. Gaga was alone at the end of the long table. "Oh? Where did everyone go?"
Wearing their crown, Gaga called, "Let us play kings!" Nobody came. The finest crown did not feel fun at all.
Gaga went beside Lala. "Let me play too." Lala hugged the crown and turned away. Gaga's mouth drooped. "Oh? I feel upset."
Lala traced the corners of their mouth downward with a finger. "Sharp words do this." Then the finger moved upward. "Kind words make a smile!"
Teacher Bau sat by the table. "Gaga, Lala's mouth has been turned down for a while." Gaga quietly studied Lala's face.
Gaga held Lala's crown. "I am sorry. Your crown is wonderfully shiny! One, think first! Two, find something good and say it! Three, say sorry first!" Lala's smile rose.
The friends gathered again in their crowns. Kind words returned as smiling mouths. Gaga put an arm around Lala and called, "Kind words make a smile!"
